claim: Needs clarification (clarify): core eligibility is unclear because random assignment to AI assistance and the number of logo creators are not reported.
problem: The supported status is context: AI versus human output (context_ai_vs_human). The empirical comparison rates AIGC-generated versus manually designed logos; it does not describe people receiving AI assistance in an experiment. The 50 professionals are questionnaire respondents. Missing creator counts do not make this documented output comparison a potentially eligible randomized assistance study.
evidence: creativity-codebook.md section 3 places AI-generated versus human-generated output comparisons in context. forms/c678.json studies[0].design_class and eligibility.context_class are both ai_vs_human; all three output contrasts have comparison_type ai_vs_human. Independently read the complete PDF at C:/Dropbox/Research/ai-lab/literature/creativity/Zhao (2023) - Exploring the Application and Influence of Artificial Intelligence AIGC Technolo.pdf. PDF p. 5 (printed p. 455), sections 3.1(3)-(4), identifies an online questionnaire and a sample of 50 design professionals; section 3.2 defines the comparison as AIGC-generated versus manual design and Table 1 reports logo ratings. No human-assistance allocation is described. The form incorrectly leaves eligibility.core as unclear despite this documented context design.

claim: Needs clarification (clarify) because of the Training randomization contradiction.
problem: The supported status is recommended for the core dataset (core). The open randomization issue concerns the separately recruited S2 Training cohort. S1 independently satisfies all three eligibility criteria, and the final form explicitly says that the S2 issue does not undermine paper-level eligibility. Applying that issue to the entire paper incorrectly withholds its qualifying randomized study.
